skill.name: momentic-mobile-test
skill.description: Create, run, and maintain Momentic mobile E2E tests and modules for Android and iOS. Use Momentic MCP tools for live device validation, and use direct v2 YAML edits only for high-confidence local mobile v2 changes.
skill.summary: Build and validate Momentic mobile end-to-end tests for Android and iOS.
skill.author: momentic-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown code spans, documentation links, platform prerequisites, or a defensive relative-path rule rather than executable behavior. Two findings are confirmed because the skill directly instructs users to run unpinned Momentic CLI packages through npx; no malicious intent or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: The doctor and lint instructions execute an unpinned package through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed Momentic CLI version and prefer the project-installed binary with a committed lockfile.

content.value_statement: Mobile test authoring can fail when platform rules, device state, and Momentic formats are unclear. This skill guides focused creation, validation, and maintenance workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates and updates Momentic mobile v2 tests and modules.
Guides interactive previews, step splicing, and focused validation through Momentic MCP tools.
Distinguishes Android and iOS requirements, commands, and coordinate formats.
Diagnoses device, app, WebView, timing, cache, and test-format failures.
Explains safe handling of modules, environment values, assets, and relative file references.
limitations: Requires a configured Momentic project and access to the relevant MCP tools.
Local Android testing needs Android tooling, while local iOS testing needs macOS and Xcode.
Direct YAML editing is limited to mobile v2 files with clear local patterns.
Live validation depends on available devices, simulators, app builds, credentials, and provider connectivity.

use_cases.title: Create a Mobile Test
use_cases.description: Build a focused Android or iOS flow from user-visible requirements and validate the saved steps.

use_cases.title: Repair a Failing Flow
use_cases.description: Separate test logic failures from device, app, WebView, cache, and provider problems.

use_cases.title: Maintain Shared Modules
use_cases.description: Evaluate reuse, preserve module contracts, and update shared mobile sequences with explicit approval.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Mobile Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this Momentic mobile test. Identify its platform, file version, configuration dependencies, and the smallest safe change for: [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Momentic mobile v2 test for [Android or iOS]. Cover [flow], use existing project patterns, and validate the smallest relevant range.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Test Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Momentic failure: [details]. Separate infrastructure, app, targeting, timing, cache, and format causes. Recommend evidence-based next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor with Live Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [test or module] for [goal]. Evaluate module reuse, preserve contracts, preview uncertain steps, splice validated checkpoints, and report remaining risks.

output_examples.input: Add a login confirmation to an Android test.
output: Identified the test as mobile v2 for Android.
Added a deterministic check for the signed-in screen.
Validated the changed step and its next dependent action.

output_examples.input: Investigate an iOS test that cannot find a WebView element.
output_examples.output: The result distinguishes app readiness, WebView context, and provider failures, then recommends the smallest diagnostic check.
The result compares suitable modules, verifies parameters and platform compatibility, and requests approval before changing shared behavior.

best_practices: Confirm platform, app source, provider, authentication, environment needs, and success criteria before editing.
Use native steps and deterministic checks when they express the required behavior.
Validate the smallest saved range that covers prerequisites, the change, and its next dependency.
anti_patterns: Do not edit deprecated v1 YAML directly or add generated fields to v2 files.
Do not run destructive, expensive, or non-idempotent actions without explicit approval.
Do not weaken assertions or inflate timeouts to hide application or infrastructure failures.

faq.question: Which mobile platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The skill covers Momentic tests for Android and iOS, including native and WebView automation.

faq.question: Can it edit every Momentic YAML file directly?
faq.answer: No. Direct editing is intended for clear mobile v2 changes. Deprecated v1 changes should use Momentic MCP persistence tools.

faq.question: Does it require a live device?
faq.answer: A device or simulator is required for previews and execution. Static inspection and focused YAML editing can occur without live validation.

faq.question: How does it handle risky test actions?
faq.answer: It requires approval before actions that submit, purchase, delete, send, create, or cause another non-idempotent side effect.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot infrastructure failures?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers drivers, device health, provider connectivity, WebView context, app launch, and simulator or emulator issues.

faq.question: When should modules be reused?
faq.answer: Evaluate module reuse for logical flows of about four or more repeatable steps, while preserving parameters and platform compatibility.
